longForm.heroHook: Pressurized coaxial cylinder rheometer, up to 1000 psi, -40°C to +260°C, down to 0.2 sec⁻¹.
longForm.heroLead: PVS Rheometer is a dynamic coaxial cylinder, controlled shear rate rheometer for measuring viscosity under pressure at elevated or reduced temperatures, where sample boil-off could otherwise be a problem. Brookfield describes it as suited to simulating in-process conditions on small fluid samples, in industries including chemicals, oil, food processing, polymers, and paints. Pressure range extends to 1000 psi, with a temperature range of -40°C to +260°C. An RTD temperature sensor on the inner cylinder surface measures sample temperature directly. The outer cylinder rotates at shear rates up to 1700 sec⁻¹, and the instrument measures down to 0.2 sec⁻¹ for low shear rate viscosity (LSRV) work. A robust motor reaches speeds up to 1000 RPM, with a stationary spindle inside the rotating outer cylinder. Standard construction uses Hastelloy cups and bobs. A triple annulus geometry option is available for increased sensitivity on low-viscosity fluids. The instrument is designed to meet API industry standards, and includes a safety relief valve. Rheovision software automates and controls test parameters. The footprint is 1' x 1' x 2', described by Brookfield as compact enough for site-to-site mobility.

sections.title: Pressure and Temperature Control
sections.description: Why boil-off is the problem this design addresses.
body: A volatile fluid tested at ambient pressure and elevated temperature can boil off before or during measurement, changing its composition and invalidating the result. PVS Rheometer's coaxial cylinder chamber operates under pressure specifically to prevent that — up to 1000 psi, across a temperature range of -40°C to +260°C, which Brookfield states makes it suitable for elevated or reduced temperature testing where boil-off would otherwise be an issue.

An RTD sensor mounted on the inner cylinder surface measures sample temperature directly at the point of shear, rather than inferring it from the chamber wall or an external probe. A safety relief valve is fitted as standard, addressing the operational risk of running a sealed chamber under both pressure and temperature extremes.

sections.title: Dual Geometry, One Instrument
sections.description: Why cone/plate and concentric cylinder on the same platform matters.
body: Different materials and test protocols call for different rheometer geometries — cone/plate suits certain viscosity ranges and sample volumes, concentric cylinder suits others. Buying separate instruments for each geometry means separate footprints, separate calibration routines, and separate operator training. RSO Rheometer supports both configurations on the same instrument, described by Brookfield as instrument flexibility suited to a wide range of material testing applications.

A quick connect coupling system attaches spindles without a lengthy fitting process, and automatic gap setting handles the spindle-to-plate distance that cone/plate geometry depends on for accurate shear rate calculation — a step that's traditionally manual and operator-sensitive on other instruments. Spindle barcode recognition identifies which geometry and spindle configuration is fitted automatically, reducing the chance of a test running against the wrong configuration data.

faqs.question: What is the RSX Coaxial Cylinder Rheometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's used for viscosity profiling, thixotropic response testing, yield stress determination, and creep analysis, positioned for quality control laboratories needing high throughput and precise, repeatable measurement.

faqs.question: What torque does the motor deliver?

faqs.question: What temperature range does it cover?
faqs.answer: -20°C to 180°C, via direct bath immersion or external circulation using the FTKY3 water jacket.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for production floor use?

faqs.question: How are spindles attached?
faqs.answer: Via a quick connect coupling system, with automatic recognition through spindle barcode scanning.

faqs.question: Does the stand adjust height?

faqs.question: How much sample does a test require?

faqs.question: How is RSX Coaxial Cylinder different from RSO Rheometer?

RSO supports both cone/plate and concentric cylinder geometry, with stand-alone operation and optional Rheo3000 PC control, but doesn't state the same torque or ruggedness specification.

faqs.answer: RSX-CC operates at standard pressure with a -20°C to 180°C temperature range, driven by torque. PVS Rheometer is pressurized to 1000 psi with a wider -40°C to +260°C range, built specifically for volatile or boil-off-prone samples.

sections.description: Why having both modes on one instrument matters.
body: Some rheological questions are best answered by fixing the shear rate and observing how stress responds; others need the reverse — fixing shear stress and observing the resulting shear rate, particularly around yield behavior. RSX Cone Plate runs both: controlled shear rate (rpm) and controlled shear stress (torque), named explicitly as distinct operating modes rather than one general controlled-shear description.

That distinction matters for method design. A test protocol built around controlled stress — common for yield stress work — and one built around controlled rate — common for standard flow curve generation — can both run on the same instrument without switching hardware, only the operating mode.

faqs.question: What is the RSX SST Rheometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Soft-Solids Tester for characterizing pastes, slurries, and soft solid materials, measuring creep, yield stress, and viscosity profile.

faqs.question: Why does it use vane and cross-hatch geometry instead of standard spindles?
faqs.answer: Standard smooth cone/plate or cylinder geometry can allow soft-solid or paste-like samples to slip at the measuring surface rather than shear internally, corrupting the measurement. Vane and cross-hatch geometry are used specifically to minimize that slippage.

faqs.question: What operating modes does it support?
faqs.answer: Controlled shear rate (rpm) and controlled shear stress (torque).

faqs.question: What are the core measurement types?
faqs.answer: Creep analysis, yield stress determination, and viscosity profiling.

faqs.question: How is the spindle gap set?
faqs.answer: Automatically, removing manual adjustment.

faqs.question: How are spindles recognized?
faqs.answer: Via barcode, automatically identifying and setting the correct spindle configuration.

faqs.question: What temperature control options are available?
faqs.answer: Peltier or fluid-heated.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for the production floor?
faqs.answer: Yes, described as rugged and built to withstand production floor demands while maintaining precision.

faqs.question: How much sample does a test require?
faqs.answer: A small sample volume, supporting rapid setup and cleanup.

faqs.question: How is RSX SST different from RSX Cone Plate or RSX Coaxial Cylinder?
faqs.answer: RSX SST uses vane and cross-hatch geometry specifically for soft solids, pastes, and slurries, where slippage is a problem on smooth cone/plate or cylinder geometry. RSX Cone Plate and RSX Coaxial Cylinder are built for standard flowable materials, with torque motors stated at 200 mNm and 200 Nm respectively.

faqs.question: How is RSX SST different from RSO Rheometer?
faqs.answer: RSO supports cone/plate and concentric cylinder geometry with stand-alone touchscreen operation, suited to standard-condition fluids. RSX SST is purpose-built with vane and cross-hatch geometry specifically for materials that slip on those standard geometries.

faqs.question: What is the price of the RSX SST Rheometer in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the spindle geometry and temperature control method required.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Ametek Brookfield RSX SST Rheometer in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroHook: Soft-solids tester, controlled shear rate and shear stress, vane and cross-hatch geometry.
longForm.heroLead: RSX SST Rheometer is built specifically for testing pastes, slurries, and soft solids — materials that fixed cone/plate or coaxial cylinder geometry can struggle with, either through slippage at the sample surface or migration of the sample out of the measuring gap. Brookfield names creep analysis, yield stress determination, and viscosity profiling as the instrument's core measurements, running in both controlled shear rate (rpm) and controlled shear stress (torque) modes. Vane and cross-hatch spindle geometries are used specifically to minimize slippage in soft-solid and paste-like samples. A quick connect coupling system attaches spindles, with automatic gap setting and spindle barcode recognition. Temperature control runs through Peltier or fluid-heated options. Construction is described as rugged, built for production floor conditions, with a large touchscreen interface.

sections.title: Why Vane and Cross-Hatch Geometry
sections.description: The slippage problem this design solves.
body: Standard cone/plate or smooth cylinder geometry works because the sample shears cleanly against the measuring surface. Pastes, slurries, and soft solids often don't behave that way — instead of shearing internally, the material slips at the surface of a smooth spindle or plate, which corrupts the measurement without necessarily looking wrong to the operator.

RSX SST addresses that specifically with vane and cross-hatch spindle geometries, described by Brookfield as used specifically to minimize slippage in soft-solid and paste-like samples. A vane geometry effectively traps material between its blades so the sample shears against itself rather than against a smooth surface; cross-hatch geometry provides a textured surface with the same intent.
